MALAYSIA: On 26 May between 0300 and 0700 local time, an unknown number of robbers boarded the Panama-flagged bulk carrier CORINTHIAN PHOENIX underway in the Singapore Strait, near position 01-26N 104-30E. Duty crew conducting routine rounds found that the storeroom had been broken into and ship?s properties were missing. The ship reported the theft to the local authorities.

INDONESIA: (Late Reporting) On 29 May at 2300 local time, four robbers armed with knives boarded the underway Singapore-flagged bulk carrier NORD ADRIATIC in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-04N 103-42E. They restrained the chief engineer and stole his personal items. The chief engineer managed to free himself and alert the bridge. The crew mustered and searched the ship. The crew discovered that ship?s stores had been stolen. The master confirmed the crew safe and the ship continued its voyage to Vietnam.

MALAYSIA: On 28 May at 2359 local time, three robbers boarded a barge under tow by the tug JIN HWA 47 in the westbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-12N 103-32E. While onboard, the perpetrators stole scrap metal. The master sounded the alarm and the crew mustered. All crew members were reported safe and the vessel continued its voyage to Penang, Malaysia.

INDONESIA: On 3 June at 0400 local time, three perpetrators armed with knives boarded the Panama-flagged bulk carrier HOANH SON GALAXY while underway in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-16N 104-16E. The master reported the duty crew had discovered intruders in the engine room after which he sounded the alarm and mustered the crew. The perpetrators escaped in a small boat off the ship?s stern. The master confirmed that nothing had been stolen and that crew members were safe. The vessel did not require any assistance and continued its voyage to China.

PERU: On 3 June at 0340 local time, robbers boarded the anchored Hong Kong-flagged product tanker BOCHEM LONDON at Callao Anchorage near position 12-00S 077-11W. The duty crew spotted the robbers near the forecastle store and raised the alarm. The perpetrators, seeing the alerted crew, escaped with stolen ship?s stores.

MALAYSIA: On 3 June at 0300 local time, robbers boarded the Panama-flagged bulk carrier ORANGE HARMONY while anchored in the Singapore Strait, near position 01-17N 104-01E. The robbers boarded the vessel unnoticed as the crew conducted bunkering and stores replenishment operations. The crew detected the theft of engine spares after the ship?s departure from the anchorage. During a search of the vessel, the crew noted footprints on the poop deck. The ship reported the incident to the Singapore Coast Guard

OMAN: On 4 June at 1235 UTC, three small craft with armed persons onboard approached a vessel underway in the Arabian Gulf approximately 14 NM north-northwest of Khasab Port, near position 26-26N 056-11E. The vessel conducted evasive maneuvers. After 30 minutes, the craft departed the area.

PHILIPPINES: On 5 June at 2300 local time, robbers armed with knives boarded the anchored Liberia-flagged container ship MERKUR HORIZON at Manila Anchorage, near position 14-36N 120-50E. The master confirmed that the perpetrators had boarded unnoticed and stolen a welding machine, two spare fire nozzles and a spanner. All crew members were safe and the ship did not require any assistance.

NIGERIA: On 5 June, at an unspecified time and location, pirates attacked two passenger boats each carrying twelve persons while underway from Abonema to Kula in the Akuku-Toru Local Government Area, Rivers State. Most of the passengers jumped into the river to avoid being abducted, which allowed the pirates to escape with both passenger boats. One female passenger, who was initially reported to have been kidnapped, was later confirmed killed. A spokesperson for the state police confirmed the incident and stated that investigations were ongoing.

ECUADOR: On 10 June at 0215 UTC, robbers in speedboats came alongside the underway Germany-flagged container ship CALLAO EXPRESS approximately 17 NM off the coast and 53 NM west-southwest of Guayaquil, near position 02-54S 080-33W. The robbers attempted to board using ladders. The alarm was raised, deck lights illuminated, crew mustered, and the master conducted evasive maneuvers. The master informed the Ecuadorian Coast Guard, which dispatched a patrol vessel to the location. When the perpetrators spotted the patrol vessel, they aborted their attempt to board and departed the area.

INDONESIA: On 11 June at 0135 local time, four robbers with knives boarded the underway Belgium-flagged bulk carrier CL CENTURY in the Phillip Channel of the Singapore Strait, near position 01-08N 103-28E. The crew spotted the robbers in the steering gear room. After discovery, the robbers escaped empty-handed. All crew reported safe. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its passage to Mozambique.

INDONESIA: On 12 June at 0130 local time, one robber armed with a shovel-like weapon boarded the underway Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier ARIANA in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-11N 103-24E. The crew discovered the robber in the steering gear room. When spotted, the robber escaped. Nothing was reported stolen and all crew are safe. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to Brazil.

INDONESIA: On 13 June at 0304 local time, three robbers armed with knives boarded the underway Liberia-flagged bulk carrier PANTAGRUEL in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-05N 103-35E. The duty crew spotted the robbers in the engine room after which the master locked down the vessel. The master checked crew numbers and their safety. The crew conducted a search of the ship, which confirmed the perpetrators had escaped empty-handed. The ship reported all crew safe.

INDONESIA: On 16 June at 2350 local time, robbers boarded the underway Vietnam-flagged offshore supply vessel HAI DUONG 55 in the eastbound lane of the Malacca Strait TSS, near position 01-12N 103-22E. After the vessel?s closed-circuit television captured suspicious movement on the main deck, the master raised the alarm and mustered the crew. A search of the vessel revealed no further sightings of the perpetrators. The master confirmed that items from a container and a coil of mooring rope had been stolen. The vessel reported all crew safe. Upon arrival in Singapore on 17 June, the master reported the incident to the local agent and the port operations control center.

INDONESIA: On 19 June at 0445 local time, four robbers armed with knives boarded the underway Philippines-flagged bulk carrier VINCENT TRADER in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-16N 104-12E. Duty crew sighted the four perpetrators in the engine room. The master sounded the alarm, mustered the crew, and had the crew conduct a security search. The master reported no further sighting of the perpetrators. One crewman was injured and engine spares were stolen. The ship continued its voyage to South Korea.

PERU: On 21 June at 0001 local time, robbers boarded the anchored Liberia-flagged bulk carrier CAIPIRINHA at Callao Anchorage, near position 12-02S 077-11W. Robbers stole ship?s stores before escaping unnoticed. The duty crew discovered the theft during routine rounds and the ship reported the incident to the local agent.

GUINEA: On 22 June at 0435 local time, four armed robbers boarded an anchored cargo ship approximately 14 NM south of Conakry, near position 09-13N 013-50W. They used force to steal money from the ship?s safe and escaped. All crew were reported safe.

INDONESIA: On 22 June at 0305 local time, two perpetrators armed with knives boarded an underway tanker in the Phillip Channel of the Singapore Strait, near position 01-04N 103-42E. The master reported no items stolen. All crew were safe and accounted for. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to Singapore.

INDONESIA: On 24 June at 0030 local time, four robbers boarded the underway Hong Kong-flagged bulk carrier BONNY ISLAND in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-16N 104-11E. The duty crew had discovered the robbers in the engine room and the master confirmed that all perpetrators had departed the vessel. No injuries occurred to the crew, and the vessel did not require assistance. The master reported engine spare parts stolen. The ship continued its voyage to South Africa.

NIGERIA: On 26 June at 1800 local time, perpetrators kidnapped eight oil workers off a passenger boat transiting through Lagos Lagoon toward Tin Can Island, near position 06-25N 003-21E. The perpetrators forced the oil workers onto their vessel and fled the area. The passenger boat was later found at a jetty in the northeast part of the Lagos Lagoon. Police confirmed the incident and have launched a manhunt for the suspected kidnappers.

YEMEN: On 27 June at 0921 local time, two skiffs with up to six persons armed with guns onboard each skiff approached to within 50 meters on the port side of an underway tanker approximately 20 NM west of Al Hudaydah, near position 14-46N 042-34E. No shots were fired. The vessel increased speed and commenced evasive maneuvers, resulting in the skiffs departing the area. The tanker and crew are safe.

INDONESIA: On 27 June at 0300 local time, three perpetrators armed with steel bars boarded an anchored tanker at Dumai Inner Anchorage, near position 01-42N 101-28E. Duty crew noticed the perpetrators near the engine room. The perpetrators threatened to attack a crewman, but he escaped. The bridge raised the alarm and the crew mustered. The perpetrators, aware of the crew?s alertness, escaped. The crew conducted a search and reported nothing missing. The local agent notified authorities of the incident.

INDONESIA: On 26 June at 2215 local time, one perpetrator boarded the underway Iran-flagged bulk carrier DARYABAR in the Phillip Channel of the Singapore Strait, near position 01-03N 103-35E. The master reported all crew safe and accounted for, and that no items had been stolen. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to China.

GHANA: On 28 June at 0055 local time, three robbers boarded an anchored cargo ship at Takoradi Anchorage, near position 04-53N 001-38W. The robbers were seen lowering paint buckets down the side of the vessel into a boat. The alarm was raised, crew mustered, and port control was notified. Following a search of the ship it was discovered that ship?s stores had been stolen, including twelve drums of paint.

CAMEROON: On 30 June at 2345 local time, perpetrators kidnapped five crew members from the anchored Panama-flagged general cargo ship OYA 1 near buoy 27 at Douala Anchorage, near position 04-00N 009-38E. The ship raised the alarm and notified the Cameroon Navy and Battalion Intervention Rapide of the incident. A patrol boat came to assist and the remaining crew are reported to be safe.

CAMEROON: On 30 June at 2240 local time, armed individuals fired upon two China-flagged fishing vessels, HAI LU FENG 13 and HAI LU FENG 14, while underway in the Wouri River near buoy 14 off Douala, near position 03-56N 009-35E. The perpetrators approached the two fishing vessels onboard several speedboats, and exchanged gunfire with members of the Cameroonian military aboard the fishing vessels. One of the perpetrators was likely killed during the exchange. The fishing vessels and crew were reported safe and sailed to Douala following the incident.

MALAYSIA: On 1 July at 2050 local time, five robbers boarded a barge under tow by a tug in the westbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-13N 103-30E. Once on the barge, the perpetrators transferred scrap metal from the barge onto two sampans. The Malaysian Marine Police from Johor subsequently detained the five perpetrators and two sampans and seized an estimated 100 tons of stolen scrap metal.

INDONESIA: On 3 July at 0345 local time, duty crew on routine rounds discovered an unauthorized person on the aft deck of a tanker anchored at Tanjung Priok Anchorage, Jakarta, near position 06-01S 106-54E. After the raising of the alarm, the crew mustered and the perpetrator escaped with his accomplices in a waiting boat. A subsequent search of the vessel found that nothing had been stolen.

INDONESIA: On 4 July at 0900 local time, four robbers boarded a barge under tow by a Malaysia-flagged tug in the westbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-16N 104-08E. The master reported seeing the robbers transferring scrap metal from the barge onto a sampan.

SIERRA LEONE: On 5 July at 0335 UTC, eight robbers boarded a fishing vessel in the northern part of Sierra Leone waters close to the border with Guinea, near position 08-53N 013-31W. The robbers stole personal belongings and ship?s stores before destroying cameras and communications equipment. During the incident, the master was shot and later hospitalized in stable condition. A Sierra Leone Navy patrol boat was sent to the fishing vessel?s location and the vessel then headed to Freetown Port.

GUINEA: On 5 July at 0200 local time, six perpetrators attempted to board a tanker anchored 14 NM south of Conakry, near position 09-17N 013-45W. Duty crew spotted the perpetrators trying to board the tanker from a small boat using a ladder. Duty crew directed a light at the individuals attempting to board, causing them to flee empty-handed.

GHANA: On 10 July at 0035 local time, two robbers boarded the anchored Portugal-flagged bulk carrier UAL OSPREY at Takoradi Anchorage, near position 04-53N 001-41W. The duty crew reported that razor wire on the forward, port side had been partly removed and they spotted two perpetrators on the upper deck. The bridge sounded the alarm, the crew mustered, and the ship notified port control. Upon hearing the alarm and seeing the crew?s alertness, the perpetrators escaped into a waiting blue wooden boat. A search of the vessel confirmed that nothing had been stolen. A patrol boat arrived later at the ship?s location and checked the area surrounding the vessel, but did not find any perpetrators.

NDONESIA: On 12 July at 0300 local time, five robbers armed with knives boarded the underway Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier ATLANTIC PRESTIGE in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-05N 103-33E. The master reported all crew safe and accounted for, and that ship?s stores and spares had been stolen. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to Singapore.

INDONESIA: On 13 July at 2345 local time, duty crew noticed a wooden boat approaching an underway bulk carrier in the eastbound lane of the Malacca Strait TSS, near position 01-11N 103-23E. A number of persons attempted to board using improvised ropes. The crew alerted the bridge and the alarm was raised, which caused the perpetrators to abandon their attempt and leave the area. The ship reported crew and vessel safe and continued its transit to China.

INDONESIA: On 15 July at 2117 local time, four robbers boarded the underway Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier TOMINI ROYALTY in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-02N 103-40E. The master reported four perpetrators in the boiler room who escaped after crew sounded the alarm. All crew reported safe with no injuries, and engine spares were reported stolen. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to Singapore.

INDONESIA: On 15 July at 0210 local time, five perpetrators boarded the underway Cyprus-flagged bulk carrier EFRAIM A in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-16N 104-14E. The crew spotted the perpetrators on the aft deck. The master sounded the alarm and mustered the crew. The crew conducted a search of the vessel, with no further sighting of the perpetrators. The ship reported all crew safe and nothing was reported stolen. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to China.

MOZAMBIQUE: On 16 July at 1230 local time, an unknown number of robbers boarded the India-flagged bulk carrier VISHVA VIKAS at Beira Anchorage, near position 19-55S 035-05E. After the robbers gained access to the vessel, they stole ship?s stores and escaped unnoticed.

INDONESIA: On 16 July at 0235 local time, five perpetrators boarded the underway Panama-flagged bulk carrier MSM in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-08N 103-27E. The crew sighted five perpetrators in the engine room. The ship sounded the alarm and the crew mustered. All crew reported safe with no injuries. The crew conducted a search onboard with no further sighting of the perpetrators. The vessel reported nothing stolen. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to Singapore.

PERU: (Late Reporting) On 18 July at 1850 local time, the duty crew of an anchored container ship at Callao Anchorage noticed a perpetrator climbing the anchor chain, near position 12-01S 077-10W. The bridge sounded the alarm and mustered the crew, which resulted in the robber abandoning the climb. The ship reported the incident to port control, which informed all vessels in the vicinity.

ANGOLA: On 20 July at 0250 local time, a number of robbers boarded an anchored container ship at Soyo Anchorage, near position 06-06S 012-12E. The robbers boarded the vessel from a small boat and stole cargo from one of the containers. The duty crew spotted the robbery in progress and raised the alarm, which resulted in the perpetrators escaping the vessel. The ship reported all crew and the vessel safe.

INDONESIA: On 20 July at 0225 local time, three perpetrators armed with knives boarded the anchored Marshall Islands-flagged tanker SUPER RUBY at Batam Anchorage, near position 01-10N 103-56E, south of the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS. After the perpetrators gained access to the vessel, the bridge raised the alarm. Seeing the crew?s alertness, the robbers escaped. The ship reported that nothing was stolen.

INDONESIA: On 22 July at 0515 local time, four unarmed robbers boarded an underway bulk carrier in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-08N 103-28E. The duty crew observed the robbers in the engine room. After conducting a search, the crew reported that engine spares had been stolen. The ship reported crew and vessel safe. The vessel did not require assistance and continued its voyage to China.

SIERRA LEONE: On 22 July at 0500 local time, 13 pirates armed with guns hijacked an underway fishing vessel approximately 19 NM southwest of Freetown, near position 08-22N 013-32W. The pirates took the fishing vessel?s 23 crew hostage and the vessel transited in a southeasterly direction toward Liberian waters. On 26 July, the International Maritime Bureau reported the Liberian Coast Guard located the hijacked fishing vessel off Monrovia, Liberia. After an exchange of gun fire between the pirates and the Coast Guard, the vessel and crew were secured. Two pirates were apprehended while the others escaped.

INDONESIA: On 22 July at 0337 local time, six robbers, one armed with a knife, boarded the underway Malta-flagged bulk carrier FIJI in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-04N 103-43E. After conducting security checks, crew members confirmed that a mobile phone and a flashlight had been stolen. The ship reported all crew safe, that it did not require assistance, and that it would continue its voyage to Singapore.

MALAYSIA: On 23 July at 2220 local time, four robbers boarded a barge under tow by a tugboat in the westbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-18N 104-10E. A Malaysian Maritime patrol boat, dispatched to the location, apprehended four Indonesian males who were unloading scrap metal from the barge.

PHILIPPINES: On 23 July at 0600 local time, the duty crew noticed the hawse pipe cover was open on an anchored LNG tanker at Batangas Anchorage, near position 13-46N 120-59E. The crew conducted a search of the vessel and reported ship?s properties stolen.

INDONESIA: On 23 July at 0350 local time, three robbers armed with knives boarded an anchored tanker at Tarahan Anchorage in southeast Sumatra, near position 05-32S 105-18E. After the duty crew reported the robbers in the engine room, the bridge raised the alarm and mustered the crew. Upon hearing the alarm, the robbers escaped with stolen engine spares. The ship reported the incident to Panjang Vessel Traffic Service after which local authorities boarded the tanker to investigate.

PERU: On 24 July at 0330 local time, the duty crew on routine rounds onboard an anchored bulk carrier at Callao Anchorage, near position 12-01S 077-12W, discovered a padlock broken and ship?s stores stolen. The crew conducted a search but no unauthorized persons were found onboard. The vessel reported the incident to port control and a patrol boat was dispatched to the ship?s location to search the area.

GHANA: On 5 August at 2352 local time, an unknown number of perpetrators onboard a canoe attempted to board a supply vessel anchored at Takoradi Anchorage, near position 04-50N 001-43W. Crew spotted the canoe as it came alongside the starboard side of the vessel. The perpetrators fled after the ship?s alarm was raised.
NIGERIA: On 5 August, an unknown number of perpetrators kidnapped two crew members from a fishing vessel operating in the vicinity of the Opobo River, near position 04-27N 007-35E.

GHANA: On 7 August at 0320 local time, five perpetrators onboard a canoe attempted to board a supply vessel anchored at Takoradi Anchorage, near position 04-50N 001-43W. The perpetrators abandoned the boarding attempt and fled after the ship?s alarm was raised. The same vessel was the target of an attempted boarding on 5 August.

INDONESIA: On 7 August at 0058 local time, one unarmed robber boarded the underway Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier JAL KAMAL in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-16N 104-16E. Crew discovered the perpetrator in the engine room. Upon being sighted, the robber fled the vessel. Following the incident, the master reported that all crew members were safe and that some main engine, generator, and fuel injection spares were missing. The ship continued its voyage to its next port of call in China.

INDONESIA: On 8 August at 2230 local time, four robbers armed with knives boarded the underway Liberia flagged bulk carrier DORIC WARRIOR in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-02N 103-39E. Crew spotted the perpetrators on the port quarter. The ship?s alarm was raised and crew mustered. A search of the ship revealed no further sign of the robbers. Main engine spare parts were reported missing. No crew members were injured during the incident. The ship reported the incident to local authorities; Singapore Police Coast Guard boarded and searched the ship after it arrived in port.

INDONESIA: On 8 August at 2036 local time, 10 robbers armed with knives and steel bars boarded a bulk carrier underway off Tanjung Balai Karimum in the Singapore Strait, near position 01-02N 103-30E. The robbers entered the engine control room, where they took the third engineer hostage and tied him up. The robbers subsequently escaped with stolen engine spares. Following the activation of the dead man alarm, the chief engineer found the third engineer tied up in the engine room and informed the master. The master raised the general alarm and reported the incident to the Singapore vessel traffic service. Singapore Coast Guard boarded the vessel to investigate the incident.

INDONESIA: On 8 August at 2150 local time, four unarmed robbers boarded the underway Liberia-flagged bulk carrier OSAKA STAR in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait TSS, near position 01-02N 103-38E. Crew discovered the perpetrators in the engine room, after which the alarm was raised and crew mustered. During a search of the ship, there was no further sighting of the robbers and main engine spare parts were discovered missing. All crew were reported safe following the incident. The ship reported the incident to local authorities; Singapore Police Coast Guard boarded and searched the ship after it arrived in port.

INDONESIA: On 9 August at 0335 local time, three unarmed robbers boarded the underway Cyprus-flagged bulk carrier SOPHOCLES GRAECIA in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-04N 103-42E. Crew discovered the perpetrators in the engine room. The alarm was raised and crew mustered. A search of the ship found no further sign of the robbers onboard. The master reported that all crew were safe and that main engine spare parts were missing. Crew conducting a subsequent security check of the vessel found a plastic molded replica toy gun. The ship reported the incident to the local authorities, Singapore Police Coast Guard boarded and searched the ship after it arrived in port.

PHILIPPINES: On 11 August at 0002 local time, eight perpetrators armed with guns boarded the Maltaflagged container ship CNC PLUTO anchored at Manila Anchorage, near position 14-35N 120-50E. They took a duty crewman hostage, tied him up, and stole his cell phone. The bridge sounded the alarm and the crew mustered. Seeing the alerted crew, the perpetrators fled the ship. The ship reported the incident to local authorities and the Philippine Coast Guard arrived and boarded the ship to investigate.

YEMEN: On 25 August, an entity impersonating the United Nations Verification and Inspection Mechanism for Yemen (UNVIM) was directing merchant vessels in the vicinity of Aden Anchorage, near position 12-48N 045-15E, to divert to Hodeidah Port in the southern Red Sea.

ERITREA: On 27 August at 1530 local time, one skiff with six people onboard approached a cargo vessel underway in the southern Red Sea, approximately 32 NM northwest of the Bab el Mandeb Strait, near position 13-05N 043-05E. The skiff, traveling at approximately 25 knots, approached to within 0.4 NM of the cargo vessel. After the armed security team onboard displayed their weapons, the skiff changed course and headed away from the vessel. The skiff was reported to be 8-12 meters long and 1-meter wide with a black/grey hull.

INDONESIA: On 29 August at 1600 local time, three robbers boarded the anchored U.S.-flagged bulk carrier SLNC SEVERN at the Belawan Port area along the Malacca Strait, near position 03-47N 098-42E. The duty crew observed them on the forecastle. The bridge raised the alarm and the crew mustered. Upon hearing the alarm, the robbers escaped with stolen ship?s stores. The ship reported the incident to local authorities through the local agent.

INDONESIA: On 1 September at 0135 local time, perpetrators boarded the underway Liberia-flagged bulk carrier YANGZE 8 in the eastbound lane of the Singapore Strait Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), near position 01-03N 103-41E. The duty crew spotted four persons, one armed with a gun-like object, in the engine room. The master requested assistance from local authorities as some crew members were unaccounted for, having locked themselves in their cabins. A subsequent search confirmed that all crew members were onboard and that no perpetrators remained on the vessel.

PERU: On 2 September at 0220 local time, four robbers armed with knives boarded the anchored Denmarkflagged tanker TORM AMALIE at Callao Anchorage, near position 12-01S 077-12W. They took one duty crewman hostage and tied him up. The bridge raised the alarm, resulting in the robbers escaping with ship?s properties and stores. After the ship reported the incident to port control, the Peruvian Coast Guard responded and boarded the vessel to investigate.

ANGOLA: On 4 September at 0312 local time, two robbers in a canoe boarded the anchored Denmark-flagged offshore supply vessel MAERSK LOGGER at Luanda Anchorage, near position 08-44S 013-18E. The duty crew on routine rounds discovered the robbers and raised the alarm, resulting in the robbers escaping with ship?s properties.

INDONESIA: On 7 September (time not specified), six robbers boarded a berthed barge at Cilacap Port on the island of Java, near position 07-44S 108-59E. Indonesian authorities apprehended one of the perpetrators and recovered two tons of coal stolen from the barge.

NIGERIA: On 11 September at 0035 local time, as many as five robbers armed with knives and steel bars boarded a berthed container ship in Lagos Port, near position 06-25N 003-21E. The robbers escaped with a high pressure machine hose. The ship reported all crew and vessel safe to the port authorities.
